_comment: signal_modulation/design01c_sweep64 — NONLINEARITY BY THE ESTABLISHED 64-PAIR AMPLITUDE-SWEEP METHOD (data_gen/generate_harmonics_data + n4_harmonics_distortion), on the design01 Nd:YAG amplifier with geometry, pump (Ez 808 from above, amp 50) and SGMA 1.86e-5 unchanged. Same protocol as the reservoir designs, so the numbers are directly comparable to them. HOW IT WORKS: sweep a parameter t over one period in 64 steps and give channel 0 the amplitude cos(3t) and channel 1 cos(5t). Each step is a SEPARATE static CW run held to steady state, so the map is memoryless by construction: output_j depends only on (A1_j, A2_j). DFT the 64 outputs at ONE optical bin: a linear amplitude map puts power only in bins 3 and 5; any nonlinearity adds DC, harmonics (6, 9, 10) and intermodulation (2, 8, 1, 7). The 3 and 5 are frequencies of the AMPLITUDE from run to run — nothing optical is swept, and computation stays at one optical frequency (user, 2026-09-01: optical-frequency mixing is a different project). CHANNELS ARE POLARISATIONS (user, 2026-09-01): both sources sit at the SAME position, SAME size and SAME wavelength 1.064, and are told apart only by polarisation — channel 0 is Ey, channel 1 is Ez. This is what makes the test sharp. In an isotropic medium in 2D, Ey and Ez decouple LINEARLY: no linear process can move power between them. The only thing that couples them is the shared inversion — both transitions have sigma_diag (1,1,1), so gain saturation depends on the total |Ey|^2 + |Ez|^2, and burning inversion with one polarisation changes the gain the other one sees. So a cos(3t) component appearing in the Ez OUTPUT (or cos(5t) in Ey) is cross-saturation with essentially zero linear background — a much cleaner signature than co-polarised channels, which are degenerate (identical position + wavelength + polarisation makes two sources exactly equivalent to one driven at A1+A2). READOUT IS THE FIELD, NOT THE INTENSITY (user, 2026-09-01: 'detecting amplitude of fields'). This is essential, not cosmetic: |E|^2 is itself a squarer and manufactures order-2 bins from a perfectly linear medium, so an intensity readout would measure the detector rather than the crystal. monitor_2 stores complex Ey and Ez per bin; take --components Ey,Ez. WHY run_until IS 3000: each run only has to reach steady state, and design01's relaxation oscillation is settled by ~2000 at every drive. AMPLITUDE: --amps 40,40 keeps each channel at +-40; unlike the co-polarised case these do not simply add, since orthogonal polarisations give a total intensity of A1^2 + A2^2 rather than (A1+A2)^2 — peak total is equivalent to a single-polarisation drive of 57, comfortably under the ceiling of 80. Created 2026-09-01 from design01.

crystal._comment: the Nd:YAG block. sted = the same 4-level Maxwell-Bloch machinery as the dyes, with Nd:YAG's lines: lbdA 0.808, lbdE 1.064, REAL linewidths. SGMA x N is the scaled doping (see top comment).

sted._comment: 4-level Nd:YAG starting FULLY INVERTED (N3_0=30, N1_0=0): the 230 us upper-level lifetime means a pre-pumped crystal simply IS in this state when a ps-scale signal arrives. SGMA 1.86e-5 = x30 the literal 1 at.% Nd:YAG value (6.2e-7), giving gL ~= 2.3 over the 20 um block — visible gain without free-running. CORRECTED 2026-09-01: the first pilot shipped SGMA 2e-3, which is gL ~= 249; the crystal dumped 97% of its inversion within 1000 t.u. REGARDLESS of drive (identical at amp 1 and amp 100) and amp 100 went non-finite at t=2281. That is parasitic free-running, not modulation. Calibration used: alpha ~ 1.1*(SGMA*N) /um at gamma=0.1, with the Lorentzian PEAK scaling as 1/gamma — the 1/gamma factor is what makes a narrow crystal line so much more sensitive to SGMA than our broad dyes (190x here).

source_1._comment: channel 0: CW Ey at 1.064 um. Amplitude is a SCALAR overwritten every run by the generator with cos(3t_j); the 1.0 is a placeholder so the design stays runnable on its own.

source_pump._comment: 808 nm CW pump entering the crystal FROM ABOVE: y-normal sheet on the crystal's top edge radiating down (SimpleSim free source placement, 2026-09-01). Ez, orthogonal to the Ey signal, so they never interfere directly; the crystal is isotropic so the pump still drives 1->4.

snap_point._comment: exit time trace, dt 0.2. Cheap at 3000 t.u. (5000 samples) and kept as the settling check: if the envelope has not flattened by dft_t_start the run is being read during the transient and every sweep point is contaminated.

pop_monitor._comment: Level populations N_l(t) AVERAGED over the crystal — the modulator's own state variable, and the cleanest read of when emission balances refill (N3 flattens). NOTE: no snap_interval on purpose. With snap_interval > 0 this sensor also stores the whole-cell snap_N (n_snaps, n_levels, Nx, Ny) + snap_E, which at 6000 t.u. is GBs per task; without it save() writes only {t, N}, the summed per-level series (sensor.py:305).

source_2._comment: channel 1: CW Ez at 1.064 um, driven with cos(5t_j). SAME position, SAME size, SAME wavelength as channel 0 — orthogonal POLARISATION is the only thing distinguishing them, which is exactly what makes cross-channel bins unambiguous (Ey and Ez do not mix linearly in an isotropic 2D medium).
